critical_question: How does updating weights using the loss gradient at a locally adversarial weight perturbation improve observed generalization beyond ordinary loss minimization, and why is that empirical benefit not an unconditional guarantee for every trained model?
source_locator: Section 2, physical pages 3-4; sections 3.1-3.3, pages 5-8; section 4, pages 8-9; whole A.1, pages 14-15; B.1 and C.3-C.4, pages 16-18, arXiv v1.
expected_relation: The approximate perturbed-gradient update targets low-loss neighborhoods rather than only pointwise loss, with broad tested generalization gains and noisy-label robustness. The theoretical bound has explicit assumptions, the implementation is approximate, and comparative gains are not uniform across every tested condition.
